newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU calls on Serbia to accept OSCE election report.
newsitem.headline: EU calls on Serbia to accept OSCE election report.

text.p: The European Union has called on Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic to accept the conclusion of an international mission that the opposition Zajedno coalition won disputed local elections in November.

Former Spanish premier Felipe Gonzalez, who headed the mission, concluded in the report to the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) that the opposition won local elections in key cities including the capital Belgrade and called on the Serbian government to honour the result.

"The European Union has noted with appreciation the report...and fully endorses the conclusions and recommendations therein," the EU said in a statement issued late on Thursday by the Dutch foreign affairs ministry. The Netherlands currently holds the EU's rotating presidency.
Milosevic's Socialists annulled the poll results sparking mass street protests which have continued for nearly two months.

"The European Union attaches particular importance to the conclusion in this report that the results...reflect the will of the majority of the citizens of Serbia and that the coalition Zajedno has won the local elections," the EU said.
"The Union...calls on the authorities...and in particular on President Milosevic, to fully accept the conclusions and recommendations (of the report) and act on them without delay," it said.
On Wednesday, Milosevic conceded the opposition Zajedno coalition had won in Serbia's second city Nis, but Zajedno leaders vowed protests would continue until all their claims were met.
The EU appealed for dialogue between the authorities and the opposition and confirmed its stance against the use of force to end the protests.
"The Union reiterates its appeal to the authorities...to refrain from the use of force against peaceful demonstrators and journalists," it said.
